$comment: Read by .github/scripts/issue_triage.js (issue-triage.yml). 'fields' maps an issue form's answer to labels: the key is the field's label (the '### Heading' GitHub writes into the issue), then each dropdown option to the labels it adds (an empty list adds none). validate_github_forms.py fails when a template's dropdown with one of these labels has an option missing here. 'checks' are the details the triage comment asks the reporter for ('ask') when an issue carrying one of 'labels' leaves them out of 'field'. Rules: 'nonempty'; 'pattern' (a JavaScript regular expression the answer must contain); 'attachment' (at least 'min' images or videos, default 1).

newIssues.$comment: Every new issue is assigned to 'assignees' (issue-triage.yml, when no one is assigned yet) and added to 'project' (add-to-project.yml). The issue forms also list both, under assignees: and projects:.

checks.ask: the exact editor version from **Help › About Scenery Editor X** (four numbers, for example `0.2.63.564`)
the end of the log file with the `[Crash]` lines (`%APPDATA%\SceneryEditorX\logs\SceneryEditorX.log`)
your graphics card and driver version
a screenshot from Scenery Editor X **and** one from X-Plane 12 of the same view
the file (zipped), a small sample that shows the problem, or the Scenery Gateway scenery ID
